evidence.title: Jorge Amado
evidence.text: Jorge Leal Amado de Faria (] , 10 August 1912 – 6 August 2001) was a Brazilian writer of the modernist school.

evidence.title: Jorge Amado
evidence.text: He remains the best known of modern Brazilian writers, with his work having been translated into some 49 languages and popularized in film, notably "Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands" in 1978.

evidence.title: Jorge Amado
evidence.text: His work reflects the image of a Mestiço Brazil and is marked by religious syncretism.

evidence.title: Jorge Amado
evidence.text: He depicted a cheerful and optimistic country that was beset, at the same time, with deep social and economic differences.

evidence.title: The Violent Land
evidence.text: The Violent Land (Portuguese: Terras do Sem Fim) is a Brazilian Modernist novel written by Jorge Amado in 1943 and published in English in 1945.

evidence.title: The Violent Land
evidence.text: It describes the battles to develop cacao plantations in the forests of the Bahia state of Brazil.

evidence.title: The Violent Land
evidence.text: Amado wrote that "No other of my books. . . is as dear to me as "The Violent Land", in it lie my roots; it is from the blood from which I was created; it contains the gunfire that resounded during my early infancy", and suggested that the novel belongs to a distinct Brazilian "literature of cacao".

evidence.title: The Violent Land
evidence.text: By 1965, the book had been adapted as a film, as well as for the stage, television and radio.

evidence.title: The Discovery of America by the Turks
evidence.text: The Discovery of America by the Turks (Portuguese: A Descoberta da América pelos Turcos) is a Brazilian Modernist novel.
evidence.resolved_title: The Discovery of America by the Turks

evidence.title: The Discovery of America by the Turks
evidence.text: It was written by Jorge Amado in 1994 but not published in English until 2012.
evidence.resolved_title: The Discovery of America by the Turks

evidence.title: The Discovery of America by the Turks
evidence.text: Amado tells how, in 1991, he was approached by an organization in Italy to write a story to celebrate the fifth centennial of the discovery of the American continent.
evidence.resolved_title: The Discovery of America by the Turks

evidence.title: The Discovery of America by the Turks
evidence.text: This would be published in a book, together with stories by Norman Mailer and Carlos Fuentes, which would be handed out to passengers flying between Italy and Central, North and South America in 1992, the year of the fifth centennial.

evidence.title: The Discovery of America by the Turks
evidence.text: Amado submitted The Discovery of America by the Turks but the Italian book was never published, leaving Amado free to publish the 77-page story as a separate volume.

evidence.title: Ilhéus Jorge Amado Airport
evidence.text: Ilhéus/Bahia-Jorge Amado Airport (IATA: IOS, ICAO: SBIL) , is the airport serving Ilhéus, Brazil.

evidence.title: Ilhéus Jorge Amado Airport
evidence.text: Since March 12, 2002 it is named after the writer Jorge Amado de Faria (1912–2001), who was born in the nearby city of Itabuna.

evidence.title: Sea of Death
evidence.text: Sea of Death (Portuguese: Mar Morto) is a Brazilian Modernist novel written by Jorge Amado.

evidence.title: Sea of Death
evidence.text: Amado wrote the novel in response to his first arrest for "being a communist".

evidence.title: Sea of Death
evidence.text: The novel follows the lives of poor fishermen around Bahia, and their relationship with the Afro-Brazilian religion Candomblé, especially the sea goddess Iemanjá.

evidence.title: Sea of Death
evidence.text: The novel's style and themes include many traits that characterize Amado's later work.

evidence.title: Blue Denim
evidence.text: Blue Denim was a successful Broadway play by writer James Leo Herlihy, the author of the novels "All Fall Down" (1960) and "Midnight Cowboy" (1965).

evidence.title: Blue Denim
evidence.text: It starred Carol Lynley, Warren Berlinger and newcomer Burt Brinckerhoff in the lead male role.

evidence.title: Blue Denim
evidence.text: Opening on February 27, 1958, the play ran for 166 performances at the Playhouse Theatre.

evidence.title: Jubiabá
evidence.text: Jubiabá (] ) is a Brazilian modernist novel written by Jorge Amado in 1935.

evidence.title: Jubiabá
evidence.text: It earned Amado an international reputation, being hailed by Albert Camus as “a magnificent and haunting” book.

evidence.title: Zélia Gattai
evidence.text: Zélia Gattai Amado de Faria (July 2, 1916 – May 17, 2008) was a Brazilian photographer, memoirist, novelist and author of children's literature, as well as a member of the Brazilian Academy of Letters.

evidence.title: Zélia Gattai
evidence.text: She was married to internationally famous writer Jorge Amado from 1945 until his death in 2001.

evidence.title: James Leo Herlihy
evidence.text: James Leo Herlihy ( ; February 27, 1927 – October 21, 1993) was an American novelist, playwright and actor.

evidence.title: Elsimar M. Coutinho
evidence.text: Elsimar Metzker Coutinho (Pojuca, May 18, 1930) is a Brazilian scientist of Luso-Austrian descent, professor, gynecologist and television personality, and character named as "Prince of Itapoan", in the books of Jorge Amado which references the Coutinho family's land in Itapoan where Amado himself lived.
